L000047

L000054	\begin{abstract}
L000055	    Using $(10087 \pm 44) \times 10^6$ $J/\psi$ events collected with the BESIII detector at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s}=3.097$ GeV,
L000056	    the antihyperon-nucleon annihilation processes $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^+ \pi^+ \pi^- + k\pi^0$ ($k=1,2,3$)
L000057	    are studied at an incident $\bar{\Lambda}$ momentum of approximately 1.074~GeV/$c$.
L000058	    The reactions $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^+ \pi^+ \pi^- \pi^0$ and $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^+ \pi^+ \pi^- 2\pi^0$ are observed for the first time,
L000059	    with corresponding cross sections $\sigma_{\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^+ \pi^+ \pi^- \pi^0} = 8.5^{+1.2}_{-1.1}~(\rm{stat.}) \pm 0.4~ (\rm {syst.})$~mb
L000060	    and $\sigma_{\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^+ \pi^+ \pi^- 2\pi^0} = 7.9^{+1.9}_{-1.7} \pm 0.4$~mb.
L000061	    No significant signal is found for $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^+ \pi^+ \pi^- 3\pi^0$, and an upper limit of 7.2 mb is set at a 90\% confidence level.
L000062	    An evidence for the $K^{*}(892)^+$ resonance is seen in the $K^+\pi^0$ invariant mass spectrum $M_{K^+\pi^0}$ for $k=1$,
L000063	    and the corresponding cross section for $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^{*}(892)^+ \pi^+ \pi^-$ is measured to be
L000064	    $\sigma_{\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^{*}(892)^+ \pi^+ \pi^-} = 12.5^{+3.8}_{-3.4} \pm 1.2$ mb.
L000065	    Owing to the limited statistics, possible interference effects are not considered.
L000066	    These findings offer crucial input to deepen our understanding of the antihyperon-nucleon interactions.
L000067	\end{abstract}
L000068	
L000069	\maketitle
L000070	
L000071	
L000072	One goal of low-energy Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) is to provide a unified and quantitative description of hadron-hadron interactions.
L000073	For the nucleon-nucleon system, decades of precise scattering data have enabled high-accuracy potential models and chiral effective field theory (chiral EFT) descriptions that underpin modern nuclear structure and reaction theory,
L000074	with growing support from lattice QCD~\cite{Machleidt2011,Epelbaum2009,Wiringa1995}.
L000075	Extending this understanding to systems with strangeness is essential for testing SU(3)-flavor aspects of the strong interaction,
L000076	constraining hypernuclear structure and spectroscopy, and determining the equation of state (EoS) of dense baryonic matter.
L000077	The latter is believed to play an important role in the so-called hyperon puzzle of neutron stars~\cite{Oertel2017,Demorest2010,Antoniadis2013,Cromartie2020,Lonardoni2015}.
L000078	Considerable progress has been made in the hyperon-nucleon (YN) sector through chiral EFT, SU(3)-based potentials, and lattice QCD,
L000079	together with input from scattering, hypernuclear spectroscopy,
L000080	and femtoscopy measurements~\cite{Haidenbauer2013,Gal2016,Rijken2010,Tolos2020}.
L000081	In contrast, the antihyperon-nucleon ($\rm \bar{Y}N$) interaction remains poorly known,
L000082	with only limited theoretical and experimental constraints available to date, though related insights can be indirectly gained from studies of $p\bar{p}$ annihilation to $\rm \bar{Y}Y$~\cite{Barnes:1987aw, Barnes:1990wh, Timmermans:1992fu, Haidenbauer:1992hv, Kohno:1987uj}.
L000083	
L000084	Extensive studies of nucleon-antinucleon interactions, from low-energy $\bar{p}p$ and $\bar{p}\rm N$
L000085	scattering to antiprotonic atoms, show a strongly absorptive,
L000086	short-range interaction well described by complex optical potentials and characterized by prolific multi-meson annihilation channels~\cite{Friedman2007}.
L000087	Theoretical investigations also emphasize that experimental measurements of the $\rm \bar{Y}N$ annihilation cross-sections provide unique insights that are complementary to those obtained from YN interactions. While YN scattering primarily probes the real part of the optical potential, the $\rm \bar{Y}N$ annihilation channels offer a direct constraint on the imaginary part, representing the absorption mechanism in the nuclear medium~\cite{Friedman2007}. These data are crucial for testing the validity of $G$-parity transformation in the strangeness sector.
L000088	Furthermore, the annihilation dynamics at low energies serve as a sensitive probe for the partial restoration of chiral symmetry and many-body effects in dense hadronic matter, which are essential for refining theoretical models of hyperon-nuclear systems~\cite{Friedman2007}.
L000089	Although these systems provide benchmarks for antibaryon-matter interactions,
L000090	direct constraints on $\rm \bar{Y}N$ dynamics are hindered by the lack of effective antihyperon beams.
L000091	By analogy, near threshold one expects similarly strong absorption and multi-meson annihilation in the strange sector, rendering the effective $\rm \bar{Y}N$ interaction highly complex in nuclear matter. Such dynamics have implications for transport and hadronization in heavy-ion collisions,
L000092	strange-antibaryon survival, light antinuclei formation and breakup, and the use of antibaryons as probes of nuclear media~\cite{Tolos2020,Friedman2007}.
L000093	To date, elastic scattering $\bar{\Lambda} p\to \bar{\Lambda} p$ is the only measured $\rm \bar{Y}N$ process~\cite{BESIII:2024geh};
L000094	no inelastic or annihilation data exist.
L000095	Therefore, dedicated $\rm \bar{Y}N$ scattering measurements are urgently needed to deepen our understanding of the $\rm \bar{Y}N$ interaction and provide
L000096	complementary insights on the YN interaction.
L000097	
L000098	Electron-positron facilities offer a unique path forward by producing hyperon-antihyperon pairs with well-defined kinematics in
L000099	two-body decays.
L000100	At BESIII, $J/\psi \to \Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$ decays deliver an intense,
L000101	quasi-monoenergetic flux of $\bar{\Lambda}$ hyperons with momentum $1.074~\mathrm{GeV}/c$ and
L000102	a spread of $\pm 0.017~\mathrm{GeV}/c$, arising from the $\pm 11~\mathrm{mrad}$ horizontal crossing angle of the $e^{+}e^{-}$ beams,
L000103	providing a clean and intensive source of antihyperons~\cite{Li2017haibo}.
L000104	In this Letter, we present the study of the
L000105	$\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-} + k\,\pi^{0}$ reactions with $k=1,2,3$ and search for possible intermediate resonances in the final states,
L000106	using a recently developed technique~\cite{Dai:2024myk,Yuan:2021yks}, which has been employed in recent pioneering BESIII analyses~\cite{BESIII:2023clq,BESIII:2023trh,BESIII:2024geh,BESIII:2025bft}.
L000107	To study the reactions of interest, a data set of $(10087 \pm 44)\times 10^{6}$ $J/\psi$ events~\cite{BESIII:2021cxx} recorded with the BESIII detector
L000108	is used.
L000109	Details of the BESIII detector, a magnetic spectrometer operating at the Beijing Electron-Positron Collider (BEPCII)~\cite{Yu:2016cof},
L000110	are given in Refs.~\cite{Ablikim2010,BESIII:2020nme,Li:2017eToF,Guo:2017eToF,Cao:2020ibk}.
L000111	As the $\bar{\Lambda}$ antihyperons traverse the beam pipe,
L000112	they can interact with the surrounding material, which is composed of $^{197}\mathrm{Au}$, $^{9}\mathrm{Be}$,
L000113	and a cooling oil with composition $^{12}\mathrm{C}:{}^{1}\mathrm{H}=1\!:\!2.13$ (see Fig.~\ref{fig:beampipe}),
L000114	producing multi-meson final states with strangeness S = 1 that directly encode short-range $\rm \bar{Y}N$ dynamics and annihilation topologies.
L000115	In particular, by using the at-rest protons ($^{1}\mathrm{H}$) in the cooling oil as targets, $\bar{\Lambda}p$ annihilation
L000116	can be directly probed. This ensures a well-defined initial state for signal identification, whereas annihilation on bound nucleons in heavier nuclei would be smeared by Fermi motion.
L000117	
L000118	\begin{figure}[htbp]
L000119	    \begin{center}
L000120	    \begin{overpic}[width=0.5\textwidth]{./diagram-20250629.pdf}
L000121	    \end{overpic}
L000122	    \end{center}
L000123	    \vspace{-0.9cm}
L000124	    \caption{
L000125	        Schematic diagram of the beam pipe and the $\bar{\Lambda}$ annihilation trajectory inside the target; the length units are centimeters (cm).
L000126	        $O$ is the interaction point of the $e^+ e^-$ collision.
L000127	        The horizontal axis is the $e^+e^-$ beam line, and the vertical axis ($r$ axis) denotes the transverse distance from the beam line.
L000128	        $\theta$ is the angle between the incident $\bar{\Lambda}$ antihyperon and the $z$ axis.
L000129	    }
L000130	    \label{fig:beampipe}
L000131	\end{figure}
L000132	
L000133	Using a {\sc geant4}-based~\cite{G42002iii} Monte Carlo (MC) package,
L000134	simulated samples are produced, incorporating the geometric description of the BESIII detector,
L000135	the propagation of particles through the detector and the detector response.
L000136	An inclusive MC sample containing 10 billion generic $J/\psi$ decays is used to investigate potential backgrounds.
L000137	The formation of the $J/\psi$ resonance is simulated by the MC event generator {\sc kkmc}~\cite{Jadach2001},
L000138	where the beam-energy spread and initial-state radiation in the $e^+ e^-$ annihilation are taken into account.
L000139	The known decay modes are generated by {\sc evtgen}~\cite{Lange2001,*Ping2008} using branching fractions taken from
L000140	the Particle Data Group (PDG)~\cite{PDG}, while the unknown decay modes are modeled with {\sc lundcharm}~\cite{Chen2000,*Yang2014a}.
L000141	The signal processes considered in this analysis are $J/\psi \to \Lambda \bar{\Lambda}$ with $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-} + k\,\pi^{0}$, with $k=1,2,3$
L000142	and $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^{*}(892)^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$, $K^{*}(892)^{+}\to K^+ \pi^0$, $\pi^0\to \gamma \gamma$.
L000143	In the signal simulation, the angular distribution of $J/\psi\to\Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$ is generated according to the measurement in Ref.~\cite{BESIII:2022qax}, and the mass and the width of $K^{*}(892)^{+}$ are set to be $891.67\pm0.26$~MeV/$c^2$ and $51.4\pm0.8$~MeV/$c^2$~\cite{PDG}.
L000144	The reactions $\bar{\Lambda}p\to  K^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-} + k\,\pi^{0}$ are simulated with the proton at rest,
L000145	with the angular distributions of the final state mesons following an isotropic phase-space distribution. The efficiency differences among the various data-taking periods are taken into account in the MC simulation, and the same event selection criteria are applied to both data and MC samples in this Letter.
L000146	
L000147	To investigate the signal process, we tag the $\Lambda$ hyperon via its decay mode $\Lambda \to p \pi^-$ (single-tag (ST)),
L000148	from which we determine the four-momentum of the $\bar{\Lambda}$ antihyperon by missing kinematics.
L000149	The signal processes are then reconstructed from the remaining tracks and neutral showers in the BESIII calorimeter not used in the tag selection.
L000150	Candidate events in which the $\bar{\Lambda}$ annihilates with a proton into $K^{+}\pi^{+}\pi^{-} + k\,\pi^{0}$
L000151	and the $\Lambda$ decays into the tag mode are called secondary annihilation (SA) events.
L000152	The cross section of the signal process is given by
L000153	\begin{equation}
L000154	\label{equ:crosssection}
L000155	    \sigma = \frac{M}{N_{A} \cdot \rho_{T} \cdot l} \cdot \frac{N_{\rm SA}}{\epsilon_{\rm sig} \cdot N_{\rm ST}} \cdot \frac{1}{{\mathcal B}^{k}_{\pi^0 \to \gamma\gamma}},
L000156	\end{equation}
L000157	where $M=1.00794$~g/mol and $\rho_T = 0.1221$~g$\cdot$cm$^{-3}$ are the molar mass and density of hydrogen in the cooling oil, respectively,
L000158	and ${N}_{\rm ST}$ and ${N}_{\rm SA}$ are the ST and SA yields.
L000159	Here, $\epsilon_{\rm sig} = \epsilon_{\rm SA}/\epsilon_{\rm ST}$ denotes the signal efficiency in the presence of
L000160	an ST $\Lambda$ hyperon, with $\epsilon_{\rm ST}$ and $\epsilon_{\rm SA}$ denoting ST and SA efficiencies, respectively,
L000161	$N_A = 6.02214076 \times 10^{23}$~mol$^{-1}$ is Avogadro’s number~\cite{Tiesinga:2021myr},
L000162	and the parameter $l = 0.5509$~mm is the average path length of the incident $\bar{\Lambda}$ in the beam pipe cooling oil.
L000163	The latter is denoted ``CD" in Fig.~\ref{fig:beampipe},
L000164	and can be extracted from MC simulations with high precision.
L000165	$\mathcal{B}^k_{\pi^0 \to \gamma \gamma}$ is the branching fraction of the decay $\pi^0 \to \gamma \gamma$, raised to the $k$-th power,
L000166	where $\mathcal{B}_{\pi^0 \to \gamma \gamma} = (98.823\pm0.034)\%$~\cite{PDG}.
L000167	
L000168	Charged tracks detected in the multilayer drift chamber (MDC) are required to be within a polar angle
L000169	range of $|\rm{cos\theta}|<0.93$, where the polar angle $\theta$ is defined with respect to the $z$-axis,
L000170	which is the symmetry axis of the MDC.
L000171	According to the MC simulation, the momenta of the proton and pion from $\Lambda$ decay are well separated:
L000172	all pions have momenta below 500 MeV/c, while protons have momenta above 500 MeV/c.
L000173	Thus, on the tag side, the charged tracks with momentum larger than 500 MeV/c are considered as proton candidates, and
L000174	otherwise as pion candidates.
L000175	
L000176	The $\pi^0$ candidates are formed by $\gamma\gamma$ pairs, where the photons are identified from showers in the electromagnetic calorimeter (EMC).
L000177	The deposited energy of each shower is required to be larger than 25~MeV in the barrel region ($|\cos\theta| < 0.80$) and larger than 50~MeV in the end-cap region ($0.86 < |\cos\theta| < 0.92$), following the standard BESIII photon selection criteria~\cite{BESIII:2023edk, BESIII:2021rqk}.
L000178	To suppress electronic noise and energy deposits unrelated to the event, the EMC time of the photon candidate relative to the event start time is required to be within [0, 700]~ns, consistent with the BESIII standard selection~\cite{BESIII:2023edk, BESIII:2021rqk}.
L000179	The $\gamma\gamma$ pairs with invariant mass in the range $[0.115, 0.150]$~GeV/$c^2$ are regarded as $\pi^0$ candidates.
L000180	A kinematic fit constraining the $\gamma\gamma$ invariant mass to the nominal $\pi^0$ mass~\cite{PDG} (1C fit) is performed, and the updated four-momentum is used in further analysis.
L000181	
L000182	To reconstruct the tagged $\Lambda$ candidates, a vertex fit is performed using all combinations of $p$ and $\pi^-$ candidates, constraining them to a common vertex. The combinations are required to satisfy $\chi^2 < 200$ for the vertex fit, where the number of degrees of freedom is 1. In addition, the invariant mass of the $p\pi^-$ system is required to be within $[1.110, 1.121]$~GeV/$c^2$.
L000183	If there are multiple $\Lambda$ candidates, only the $p \pi^-$ combination with the minimum vertex-fit $\chi^2$ is kept.
L000184	The ST yield is then extracted from an unbinned maximum-likelihood fit
L000185	on the recoil-mass spectrum against the reconstructed $\Lambda$ candidate ($RM_{\Lambda}$),
L000186	which is defined as
L000187	\begin{equation}
L000188	    RM_{\Lambda} =
L000189	    \sqrt{(E_{\rm cms}-E_{p \pi^-})^2/c^4 - \vec{p}_{p\pi^-}^2/c^2}.
L000190	    \label{Eq:mRec}
L000191	\end{equation}
L000192	Here, $E_{\rm cms}$ is the center-of-mass energy, $E_{p \pi^-}$ and $\vec{p}_{p \pi^-}$
L000193	are the energy and momentum of the tagged $p \pi^-$ in the $J/\psi$ rest frame, respectively.
L000194	In the fit, the signal is modeled using the shape of  MC samples convolved with a Gaussian function,
L000195	which accounts for the difference
L000196	in the mass resolution between data and MC simulation.
L000197	The background shape is described by a third-order Chebyshev polynomial.
L000198	The fit to the $RM_{\Lambda}$ distribution is shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:SingleTag};
L000199	the red arrows denote the signal region, $RM_{\Lambda}$ $\in$ [1.071, 1.160]~GeV/$c^2$,
L000200	and the corresponding ST yield is determined to be $N_{\rm ST} = (7511.4 \pm 3.6) \times 10^{3}$.
L000201	
L000202	\begin{figure}[htbp]
L000203	    \begin{center}
L000204	        \begin{overpic}[width = 0.8\linewidth]{./mRecLambda-eps-converted-to.pdf}
L000205	        \end{overpic}
L000206	    \end{center}
L000207	    \vspace{-0.6cm}
L000208	    \caption{
L000209	        Fit to the $RM_{\Lambda}$ distribution for the ST sample.
L000210	        The dots with error bars are data, the blue solid line is the total fit,
L000211	        the red long-dashed and green short-dashed lines denote the fitted signal and background shapes.
L000212	    }
L000213	    \label{fig:SingleTag}
L000214	\end{figure}
L000215	
L000216	
L000217	Signal processes $\bar{\Lambda} p \to K^+ \pi^+ \pi^- + k\,\pi^0$ are identified from the remaining charged tracks and $\pi^0$ candidates
L000218	after reconstructing the tagged $\Lambda$ candidates.
L000219	Particle identification (PID) for these charged tracks combines measurements of the specific ionization energy loss in the MDC ($\mathrm{d}E/\mathrm{d}x$)
L000220	and the flight time in the time-of-flight system to form likelihoods $\mathcal{L}(h)(h = p, K, \pi)$ for various hadron hypotheses $h$.
L000221	Charged tracks with $\mathcal{L}(K)>\mathcal{L}(\pi)$ are identified as kaons, and pions are required to satisfy $\mathcal{L}(\pi)>\mathcal{L}(K)$.
L000222	A vertex fit is performed on all the $K^+ \pi^+ \pi^-$ combinations to obtain the vertex position of the $\bar{\Lambda} p$ interaction.
L000223	If there are multiple $K^+ \pi^+ \pi^-$ candidates, only the one with the smallest $\chi^2$ is retained for further analysis.
L000224	To select the best $\pi^0$ candidate for the three signal topologies,
L000225	we minimize $\chi^2_{1\mathrm{C}}(\pi^0)$ for $k=1$,

L000235	The three-momentum of the struck proton is inferred from momentum conservation within the reconstructed system, as

L000407	In summary, using $(10087 \pm 44)\times 10^6$ $J/\psi$ events collected with the BESIII detector,
L000408	we report the observation of the reactions $\bar{\Lambda}p \to K^+\pi^+\pi^- + k\pi^0$ with $k=1,2$,
L000409	and set an upper limit on the process $\bar{\Lambda}p \to K^+\pi^+\pi^- 3\pi^0$.
L000410	The $\bar{\Lambda}$ hyperons originate from $J/\psi \to \Lambda\bar{\Lambda}$ decays, traverse the beam pipe, and annihilate on the protons at rest in the cooling oil.
L000411	In addition, an evidence for an intermediate $K^{*}(892)^{+}$ in the $k=1$ channel is found in the invariant mass spectrum $M_{K^+\pi^0}$.
L000412	The cross sections of these signal processes are measured at $p_{\bar{\Lambda}}\simeq 1.074$~GeV/$c$ (corresponding to $\sqrt{s}\simeq2.243$~GeV),
L000413	as shown in Table~\ref{tab:cross_section}.
L000414	These measurements provide important quantitative constraints on the $\rm \bar{Y}N$ annihilation
L000415	into multi-meson final states, supply valuable input for transport and hadronization modeling in heavy-ion collisions,
L000416	including strange‑antibaryon survival and light‑antinuclei formation,
L000417	and enable tests of SU(3)-flavor symmetry via comparisons with existing $\bar{p} \rm N$ annihilation data.
L000418	Moreover, these data provide direct constraints on the imaginary part of the optical potential and
L000419	are essential for testing the $G$-parity transformation in the strangeness sector.
L000420	The same approach can be pursued at the future Super $\tau-$Charm Facility~\cite{Achasov:2023gey} for more precise,
L000421	differential investigations of the $\rm \bar{Y}N$ scattering and annihilation dynamics.
